audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the 32-byte threshold in encode_internal_node implemented correctly without off-by-one errors?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: encode_internal_node is an Execution Layer (EL) Python execution-spec MPT trie function. Target codebase is Prysm, a Consensus Layer (CL) Go client that does not implement EL MPT trie operations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is RLP encoding canonical and deterministic for all input types?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: RLP encoding is an Execution Layer (EL) concept used in MPT tries. Target codebase is Prysm (CL), which uses SSZ encoding, not RLP. No RLP trie encoding exists in this codebase.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 producing consistent, deterministic 32-byte output for all inputs?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: This checks keccak256 usage in EL MPT trie operations. Prysm (CL) uses keccak256 only for key derivation/signing, not for trie hashing. The EL trie context does not exist in this codebase.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is keccak256 collision resistance maintained for Ethereum address and storage key hashing?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: Ethereum address and storage key hashing via keccak256 in MPT trie context is an EL operation. Prysm (CL) does not implement EL state trie or storage trie operations.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_node correctly dispatch all value types through the isinstance chain without silent misclassification?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: encode_node with isinstance dispatch is a Python EL execution-spec function. Prysm (CL) is a Go codebase with no equivalent encode_node function or isinstance chain.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does the previous_trie.encode_node fallback produce semantically compatible, non-empty output?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: previous_trie.encode_node is a Python EL execution-spec cross-fork trie encoding mechanism. No equivalent exists in Prysm (CL).

audit_items.title: Does copy_trie produce a completely independent copy where modifications to one do not affect the other?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: copy_trie is a Python EL execution-spec function for deep-copying MPT tries. Prysm (CL) uses sparse Merkle tries (container/trie/sparse_merkle.go) with different copy semantics.

audit_items.title: Does trie_set with default value correctly delete existing keys from trie._data?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: trie_set is a Python EL execution-spec function operating on MPT trie._data dict. No equivalent exists in Prysm (CL) Go codebase.

audit_items.title: Is trie_set with default value a no-op when the key doesn't exist in trie._data?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: trie_set is a Python EL execution-spec function. Prysm (CL) does not implement EL MPT trie set/get operations.

audit_items.title: Does trie_get return exactly trie.default (identity, not equality) for non-existent keys?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: trie_get with Python identity semantics is an EL execution-spec function. Prysm (CL) does not implement EL MPT trie get operations.

audit_items.title: Can nibble values outside the valid range [0, 15] reach nibble_list_to_compact and cause incorrect encoding?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: nibble_list_to_compact is a Python EL execution-spec function for Hex-Prefix encoding in MPT tries. No equivalent nibble/HP encoding exists in Prysm (CL).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does nibble_list_to_compact correctly encode the is_leaf flag and parity in the header byte?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: nibble_list_to_compact HP encoding is an EL execution-spec function per Yellow Paper. No HP encoding implementation exists in Prysm (CL).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does an empty trie ({}) produce the canonical EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT (keccak256(rlp(b''))) is an EL MPT trie constant. Prysm (CL) uses sparse Merkle trees with different empty root semantics.

audit_items.title: Does patricialize with a single-element input correctly return a LeafNode with the correct key suffix?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: patricialize is a Python EL execution-spec function that builds MPT trie nodes (LeafNode, ExtensionNode, BranchNode). No equivalent exists in Prysm (CL).

audit_items.title: Does patricialize correctly create ExtensionNodes with exact shared prefix when keys share a common prefix?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: patricialize ExtensionNode creation is a Python EL execution-spec MPT trie algorithm. Prysm (CL) does not implement MPT patricia tries.

audit_items.title: Does patricialize correctly create BranchNodes with 16 subnodes when keys have no shared prefix at the current level?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: patricialize BranchNode creation with 16-way branching is a Python EL execution-spec MPT algorithm. Prysm (CL) uses binary sparse Merkle tries, not 16-ary MPT.

audit_items.title: Does patricialize correctly assert when Account/Receipt/Uint values appear in BranchNode value position?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: patricialize BranchNode value assertions for Account/Receipt/Uint types are Python EL execution-spec constructs. None exist in Prysm (CL).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does root() always return exactly 32 bytes regardless of internal root node size?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: root() with RLP encoding and keccak256 hashing for small nodes is an EL MPT trie operation. Prysm (CL) sparse Merkle trie root() has different semantics.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Can an attacker craft inputs causing pathological trie structures in unsecured tries, leading to DoS?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: Unsecured MPT tries (transactions, receipts) with pathological key patterns is an EL concept. Prysm (CL) does not process EL MPT tries.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does encode_node's isinstance chain handle all current-fork types explicitly without silent fallthrough to previous_trie?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: encode_node isinstance chain with previous_trie fallback is a Python EL execution-spec pattern. No equivalent exists in Prysm (CL) Go codebase.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Can an attacker cause unbounded state entry growth within a single block, causing root computation to exceed time limits?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: EL state entry growth and MPT root computation timing is an EL concern. Prysm (CL) does not compute EL state trie roots.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does root() correctly hash small root nodes whose RLP encoding is < 32 bytes?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: root() with RLP < 32 byte threshold hashing is an EL MPT trie operation. Prysm (CL) does not implement EL MPT root computation.

audit_items.title: Does _prepare_trie process all entries in trie._data without skipping any?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: _prepare_trie operating on trie._data is a Python EL execution-spec internal function. No equivalent exists in Prysm (CL).

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does secured trie key hashing prevent collisions that would overwrite state entries?
audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: Secured trie key hashing (keccak256 pre-hashing) for collision resistance is an EL MPT trie security mechanism. Prysm (CL) does not implement secured EL tries.

audit_items.skip_reason: Component mismatch: trie._data.items() iteration order independence is a Python EL execution-spec concern. Prysm (CL) does not implement EL MPT trie root computation with Python dicts.
